correctness.rationale: The timestamp representation gives exact marginals, nesting conditionals and the single-separator integral. Pairwise neighborhoods exhaust all possible joint configurations, with b1,b2 each O(n^{-1/2}) uniformly over fixed-size-mark families. Published AGG Theorem 2 then bounds the full marked site process; boundary probability O(n^{-1/2}); weak spatial convergence from intensity Riemann sums. Independent exact enumeration checks 5912 BST permutations and 362880 nine-rank timestamp permutations, with six joint local identities. Finite enumeration alone is not a proof.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text comparison identifies Dennert--Grübel (2010, p.576 §4.2) as an explicit unsolved multivariate critical Poisson conjecture, not a previous theorem. Holmgren--Janson 2014 states different-size joint results only when sizes are fixed; their varying-size Poisson result is marginal. The new critical-scale marked spatial total-variation theorem is strictly stronger than finite covariances or separate marginal limits. Specific same-subject primary full texts and finite prior records have been compared. General AGG Poisson approximation needs the new BST-specific nesting and one-gap collision bounds.
residual_risks: A later unlocated proof of the Dennert--Grübel §4.2 conjecture could exist; neither database search nor examined sources certify historical priority exhaustively.
Feng--Mahmoud--Panholzer (2008) was not inspected in full; its directly stated abstract results are univariate, and the later full-text sources treat its result as such.
Arbitrary growing mark sets or subtree sizes outside a compact square-root band are not covered.

value.rationale: Resolves the specific open critical-middle-range multivariate independence conjecture in Dennert--Grübel (2010, §4.2), including arbitrarily close but distinct sizes. The stronger complete rank-location marked-point-process total variation bound gives a practical uniform error and spatial calibration for simultaneous fringe subtree counts, not obtainable from one-size Poisson or covariance formulas.
